# Feature flags

A feature flag turns a feature on or off without a deploy.
You declare each flag in `spinup.toml`. Your code asks if the flag is on.
An administrator changes the flag with a command or on the page `/admin/flags`.
The `flags` module needs the `auth` module.

```console
$ spinup new todo --module example.com/todo --modules auth,flags --no-git --non-interactive
...
$ cd todo
$ spinup doctor --quick 2>/dev/null | grep flags-drift
ok	flags-drift	generated flags match [flags] in spinup.toml
```

A flag is a boolean. A change reaches every running process within 10 seconds.
The process that made the change sees it at once.
Before the first successful load, every flag has its declared `default`.
If the database goes down later, each process keeps its last snapshot until a refresh succeeds.

## Declare a flag

Add one table for each flag to `spinup.toml`.

```toml
[flags.new_checkout]
description = "The new checkout flow"
default = false
public = true
owner = "ana@example.com"
expires = "2027-03-31"
```

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | string | none | What the flag does. It is required and has 1 to 200 characters. |
| `default` | bool | `false` | The answer before the database is loaded, and the first value of a new flag. |
| `public` | bool | `false` | If true, the web pages and `GET /api/flags` get the answer. |
| `owner` | string | none | Who owns the flag. It is free text, for people only. |
| `expires` | date | none | The day you want to remove the flag, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. |

A key matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,47}$`. It has no double underscore and no trailing underscore.
An app has 64 flags at most. An unknown key in the table is an error.
See [the configuration reference](../reference/configuration.md#flagskey).

## Generate the typed keys

Run `spinup g flags` after each change to the `[flags]` tables.
The command writes a Go constant for each flag, and a TypeScript type for the public flags.
See [generate flags](../commands/generate-flags.md).

```console
$ printf '\n[flags.new_checkout]\ndescription = "The new checkout flow"\ndefault = false\npublic = true\nowner = "ana@example.com"\nexpires = "2027-03-31"\n' >> spinup.toml
$ spinup g flags
Created 0, updated 2 files
$ cat api/internal/flags/flags.gen.go
// Code generated by spinup. DO NOT EDIT.

package flags

import kitflags "github.com/stopyellingatme/spinup/kit/x/flags"

const (
	// NewCheckout is the "new_checkout" flag.
	NewCheckout = "new_checkout"
)

// Set is the flag set of this app. Pass it to flags.WithDeclared.
var Set = kitflags.Declared{
	NewCheckout: {Description: "The new checkout flow", Default: false, Public: true, Expires: "2027-03-31"},
}
$ cat web/src/lib/flags.gen.ts
// Code generated by spinup. DO NOT EDIT.
/** The public flag keys of this app. */
export type FlagKey = 'new_checkout';
/** The role that can open /admin/flags (admin_role in spinup.toml). */
export const adminRole = 'manager';
```

If you remove a flag from `spinup.toml` and run the command again, the constant goes away.
Code that still uses it does not compile. This is how a removed flag cannot stay in the code.
The `spinup doctor` check `flags-drift` warns when a generated file differs from `spinup.toml`.

## Check a flag in Go

Ask for the flag with the constant. The answer is the same for the whole request.
A check reads a snapshot in memory. It runs no SQL.

```go
import (
	appflags "example.com/todo/api/internal/flags"
	"github.com/stopyellingatme/spinup/kit/x/flags"
)

func checkout(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if flags.Enabled(r.Context(), appflags.NewCheckout) {
		newCheckout(w, r)
		return
	}
	oldCheckout(w, r)
}
```

The middleware in `api/cmd/api/main.go` finds the signed-in user for you.
The rules use the user ID and the role of that user.

In a job or a command, there is no request. Build the scope yourself:

```go
ctx = flagsProvider.Context(ctx, flags.Subject{UserID: 42, Role: "staff"})
on := flags.Enabled(ctx, appflags.NewCheckout)
```

Without a scope, `flags.Enabled` returns `false`. It does not panic.
For more detail, use `flags.Evaluate(ctx, key)`. It returns the value, the variant (`on` or `off`), and the reason.
Each check adds the span event `feature_flag.evaluation` to the trace. The event has no user ID.

## Read a flag in a page

Only the flags with `public = true` reach the web app.
The layout data of every page has them as `data.flags`. The helper `flag` reads one.
A key that is not public does not compile, because it is not in `FlagKey`.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
	import { flag } from '#lib/flags.js';

	let { data } = $props();
</script>

{#if flag(data, 'new_checkout')}
	<a href="/checkout">Try the new checkout</a>
{/if}
```

The server render and the browser read the same data, so they always agree.
The browser never gets a rule, a role list, a percentage, or a user list.
If the API fails to answer, the page renders with every public flag off.

## Change a flag

You have three ways to change a flag. All three write to the database.

| Way | Use it when |
| --- | --- |
| The app command `flags` | You work in a terminal, or in a script. |
| The page `/admin/flags` | An administrator works in the browser. |
| `PUT /api/admin/flags/{key}` | Another program must change a rule. |

### With the app command

Run the command from the `api/` folder. See [the flags command](../reference/app-commands.md#flags) for every action.

<!-- doctest: requires-env DATABASE_URL -->
```console
$ spinup db migrate up
...
$ cd api
$ go run ./cmd/api flags enable new_checkout
updated new_checkout	on
$ go run ./cmd/api flags set new_checkout --roles manager --percent 50
updated new_checkout	roles=manager percent=50
$ go run ./cmd/api flags list
...
$ go run ./cmd/api flags disable new_checkout
updated new_checkout	off
$ go run ./cmd/api flags set new_checkout --roles "" --percent 0
updated new_checkout	roles= percent=0
```

To turn a flag on or off for one account, use `flags user`:

<!-- doctest: skip -->
```console
$ go run ./cmd/api flags user new_checkout --email bob@example.com --on
updated new_checkout	bob@example.com on
$ go run ./cmd/api flags user new_checkout --email bob@example.com --clear
updated new_checkout	bob@example.com clear
```

A wrong call fails and prints a `Try:` line:

<!-- doctest: requires-env DATABASE_URL -->
```console
$ go run ./cmd/api flags set new_checkout --roles nope
flags set: flags: the role "nope" is not declared. Declared roles: manager, staff.
Try: use one of the declared roles, or add the role to [auth] in spinup.toml and run spinup g roles.
exit status 1
[exit 1]
```

On a server, open a shell on the VM and run the command in the `api` container:

<!-- doctest: skip -->
```console
$ spinup server ssh --env production
$ docker exec -i "$(docker ps --filter name=api --format '{{.Names}}' | head -n 1)" /api flags set new_checkout --percent 10
updated new_checkout	roles= percent=10
```

The command needs no web server. It writes to the database that the container uses.
Every running process reads the change within the refresh time.
Set the time with `FLAGS_REFRESH`. The default is `10s`, and the lowest value is `1s`.

### On the admin page

An account with the `admin_role` sees the link `Feature flags` in the user menu.
The page `/admin/flags` shows one row for each flag.
A row has a switch for the global value, one checkbox for each role, and a number for the percentage.
It also lists the rules for single users, and a form to add one by email address.

The page works without JavaScript. Every change posts a form.
Another role gets a 403. A visitor who is not signed in goes to the sign-in page.

### With the API

The admin routes answer only to the `admin_role`. They are not part of the OpenAPI document.

| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/admin/flags` | Lists the flags, the declared roles, and the `admin_role`. |
| `PUT /api/admin/flags/{key}` | Replaces the rule. The body needs `enabled`, `roles`, and `percentage`. |
| `PUT /api/admin/flags/{key}/users/{email}` | Sets a rule for one user. The body is `{"enabled": true}`. |
| `DELETE /api/admin/flags/{key}/users/{email}` | Removes the rule of one user. |
| `GET /api/flags` | Gives the public flags as booleans. Every visitor can call it. |

## Precedence and the percentage

For a signed-in user, the first step that decides gives the answer.
A specific rule beats a general one.

| Step | Condition | Answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | The flag is not declared. | `false` |
| 2 | The flag has no stored rule yet. | The declared `default`. |
| 3 | The user has a rule. | The value of that rule, `on` or `off`. |
| 4 | The global switch is on. | `true` |
| 5 | The role of the user is in the role list. | `true` |
| 6 | The percentage is above 0, and the bucket of the user is below it. | `true` |
| 7 | Nothing above matched. | `false` |

A rule for one user that says `off` beats a global `on`.
A signed-out visitor gets only steps 1, 2, 4, and 7. Only the global value counts.

The bucket is a number from 0 to 99. It is `FNV-1a("<key>:<user id>") % 100`.
Each flag has its own key, so each flag picks other users.
The same user always gets the same bucket for the same flag.
For example, user 42 has bucket 42 for `new_checkout`. A percentage of 42 gives `off`, and 43 gives `on`.

The percentage is not in the hash. A rise from 5 to 20 keeps every user who was on and adds more users.
A fall removes users from the top of the range only.

## Test a flag

Use `flagstest.Override` in a test. It forces a value until the test ends.

```go
import (
	appflags "example.com/todo/api/internal/flags"
	"github.com/stopyellingatme/spinup/kit/x/flags"
	"github.com/stopyellingatme/spinup/kit/x/flags/flagstest"
)

func TestCheckoutWhenOn(t *testing.T) {
	flagstest.Override(t, appflags.NewCheckout, true)
	if !flags.Enabled(context.Background(), appflags.NewCheckout) {
		t.Fatal("the flag is off")
	}
}
```

`Override` works for the whole process. Do not call `t.Parallel` in a test that overrides a key that another test overrides.

To test a handler, give the request a scope with `flagstest.Context`. Use `flagstest.ContextAs` to set a signed-in user:

```go
ctx := flagstest.Context(context.Background(), map[string]bool{appflags.NewCheckout: true})
req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/checkout", nil).WithContext(ctx)
```

A test with `flagstest` needs no database.

## Retire a flag

Set `expires` when you add a flag that you plan to remove.
When the date passes, `spinup doctor` warns:

<!-- doctest: skip -->
```console
$ spinup doctor --quick | grep -A1 flags-drift
warn	flags-drift	1 flags are past their expires date: new_checkout (2027-03-31).
Try: remove each [flags.<key>] table and its uses from the code, run spinup g flags, then flags prune --yes
```

Follow these steps:

1. Remove the uses of the flag from the code. Keep the branch that you want.
2. Remove the table `[flags.<key>]` from `spinup.toml`.
3. Run `spinup g flags`. The constant goes away.
4. Deploy the new version.
5. Run `flags prune --yes` on the server.

An old row keeps its stored value until you prune it. `flags list` marks it `stale`.
`flags prune` deletes only rows with no declaration. It never deletes a declared flag.
Without `--yes`, the command fails and deletes nothing.

<!-- doctest: requires-env DATABASE_URL -->
```console
$ go run ./cmd/api flags prune
flags prune: --yes is required, because the command deletes rows.
Try: flags prune --yes
exit status 1
[exit 1]
$ go run ./cmd/api flags prune --yes
nothing to prune
```

## The audit trail

With the [audit module](../audit.md), every change of a rule writes an event.
An administrator on the admin page is the actor. The command uses the operator of the shell.
Without the audit module, the pages show only the time of the last change.

If you add the audit module after the flags module, the database has no triggers on the flag tables.
The API logs a warning at startup: `feature_flags has no audit triggers`. The check `flags-wired` cannot always see this case, because it reads only files. Run `spinup db new audit_feature_flags`, and paste these four statements into the new file:

```sql
-- +goose Up
CREATE TRIGGER feature_flags_audit AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON public.feature_flags
    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION audit_row_change('', 'key');
CREATE TRIGGER feature_flags_audit_truncate AFTER TRUNCATE ON public.feature_flags
    FOR EACH STATEMENT EXECUTE FUNCTION audit_truncate();
CREATE TRIGGER feature_flag_users_audit AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON public.feature_flag_users
    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION audit_row_change('', 'flag_key,user_id');
CREATE TRIGGER feature_flag_users_audit_truncate AFTER TRUNCATE ON public.feature_flag_users
    FOR EACH STATEMENT EXECUTE FUNCTION audit_truncate();

-- +goose Down
DROP TRIGGER feature_flag_users_audit_truncate ON public.feature_flag_users;
DROP TRIGGER feature_flag_users_audit ON public.feature_flag_users;
DROP TRIGGER feature_flags_audit_truncate ON public.feature_flags;
DROP TRIGGER feature_flags_audit ON public.feature_flags;
```

Then run `spinup db migrate up`.

## Add flags to an existing app

Upgrade the app first. Then add the module. It makes a branch for you to review.

<!-- doctest: skip -->
```console
$ spinup upgrade --yes
$ spinup module add flags --yes --non-interactive
...
Next: git merge spinup/module-flags
```

The flags migration is in `api/db/kit/`. It does not clash with the migrations of your app.
The command prints `Next:` lines for the files that spinup does not overwrite.
These are the edits in `api/cmd/api/main.go`:

```go
var flagsEnv struct {
	Refresh time.Duration `env:"FLAGS_REFRESH" default:"10s"`
}
if err := config.Load(&flagsEnv); err != nil {
	return err
}
flagsProvider, err := flags.New(flags.WithDeclared(appflags.Set))
if err != nil {
	return err
}
flagStore := flags.NewStore(pool, flagsProvider, roles.Set)
if err := flagStore.Start(ctx, flagsEnv.Refresh); err != nil {
	return err
}
```

Put this block after `auth.New` and before `app.New`. Then add these options to `app.New`:

```go
app.WithMiddleware(authn.Middleware()),
app.WithMiddleware(flagsProvider.Middleware()), // after the auth middleware
app.WithRoutes(flagStore.Routes(authn)),
app.WithCommand("flags", flagStore.Command()),
app.WithReadiness("flags", flagStore.Ready),
app.WithShutdown(flagStore.Close),
```

The flags middleware must come after the auth middleware. If it comes before, every user is anonymous.
In the web app, `web/src/hooks.server.ts` loads `GET /api/flags` next to the session and sets `locals.flags`.
Add `flags: Record<string, boolean>` to `Locals` in `web/src/app.d.ts`, and return `flags` from `web/src/routes/+layout.server.ts`.
Pass the link `Feature flags` to `UserMenu` in `web/src/routes/+layout.svelte`.
If your files merge with conflicts, copy these blocks from a new app that has the module.

Run `spinup db migrate up` before you start the new binary.
Then run `spinup g flags` and `spinup doctor`. The default `flags.gen.ts` names `manager` as the `admin_role`. An app with other roles needs `spinup g flags`.

## Limits

- A change takes up to `FLAGS_REFRESH` (10 seconds by default) to reach another process.
- A percentage applies to signed-in users only. A signed-out visitor gets the global value. There is no rollout by percentage for visitors.
- Embed mode has no flags. The module needs `auth`, and `auth` needs the Node frontend. Use `--frontend-mode node`.
- `spinup new` needs `--modules auth,flags`. `spinup module add flags` adds `auth` for you.
- A flag is a boolean. There are no strings, numbers, or variants beyond `on` and `off`.
- The declarations live in `spinup.toml`. You cannot create a flag at run time.
- A role in a rule keeps its text if you remove the role from `[auth]`. The page marks it `undeclared`. Remove it before you reuse the name.
- A flag that you declare with a wrong key is a compile error. A wrong string in your code is not. Always use the constant.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spinup g flags` says the key does not match | The key has a capital letter, a dash, or a double underscore. | Rename the table `[flags.<key>]`. |
| `flags list` fails with a missing table | The migration did not run. | Run `spinup db migrate up`. |
| `/readyz` answers 503 with `"flags": "fail"` | The last refresh failed. | Run `spinup db migrate up`. Check the database. |
| `flags.Enabled` is always false | The code has no scope, or `main.go` lacks the middleware. | Run `spinup doctor`. See the check `flags-wired`. |
| A page does not see a flag | The flag is not `public`, or `spinup g flags` was not run. | Set `public = true` and run `spinup g flags`. |
| The change takes long to appear | The refresh time is long. | Set `FLAGS_REFRESH=1s`, or wait. |
